original_question: For every geometrically finite rational map f, is every connected component of its Julia set locally connected?
target_in_paper: §5, "Geometrically finite maps and Kleinian groups" (McMullen), under "Geometrically finite rational maps," Problem 2: "Show every component of J is locally connected."
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual problem. It correctly identifies the class of maps (geometrically finite rational maps), the object of interest (components of the Julia set), the quantifier (every component / every such map), and the property to be proved (local connectivity). Using "connected component" instead of "component" is faithful here.
missing_details: The paper defines the setting explicitly: f is a rational map on the Riemann sphere, C is its set of critical points, P = union_{n>=1} f^n(C) is the post-critical set, and J is the Julia set.
The paper's definition of "geometrically finite" is not stated in the draft: P ∩ J is finite.
The paper gives an explicit equivalent formulation that is useful for making the question stand-alone: every critical point lying in J is preperiodic.
The paper notes a hidden scope condition: rationally indifferent cycles are allowed in the geometrically finite case.

The official formulation is an open problem phrased as "Show every component of J is locally connected," not a broader neighboring conjecture about density of expanding maps or about connected Julia sets only.
refined_question: Let f be a rational map of the Riemann sphere, let C be its set of critical points, let P = union_{n>=1} f^n(C) be its post-critical set, and let J = J(f) be its Julia set. Assume that f is geometrically finite in the sense that P ∩ J is finite (equivalently, every critical point of f that lies in J is preperiodic; rationally indifferent cycles are allowed). Must every connected component of J be locally connected?
equivalent_formulation: If f is a rational map such that every critical point in its Julia set J(f) is preperiodic, are all components of J(f) locally connected?
justification: This draft is targeting McMullen's Problem 2 in §5 almost verbatim. The nearest official formulation is exactly the local-connectivity problem for components of the Julia set of a geometrically finite rational map, not the preceding density conjecture for expanding maps and not the later problem about combinatorial classification. The only paper-critical information omitted by the draft is the paper's definition of geometrically finite, the notation for the post-critical set and Julia set, and the equivalent preperiodicity formulation supplied in the surrounding context.
